messages:
ashley: Heads-up — after the pulse-window heuristic rollout at ~2149001050 I'm seeing a clear perf regression. p99 +210ms, overall throughput down ~18%. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/SRV/perf?orgId=1

diego: Can you paste the grafana panel or the short link? Any kernel-selection churn in the logs?

ashley: short link: https://grafana.internal/d/SRV/pulse-window-compare
Quick profiler snippets from the runtime logs around 2149001100:
```
[2149001102] req=aa12 kernel_selected=fast_attention_v2 shape=(1,128)
[2149001103] req=aa13 kernel_selected=generic_matmul shape=(1,128) fallback_reason=packing_cost_estimate
[2149001104] req=aa14 batch_size=2 kv_hit=false prefetch_miss=true
```
Looks like identical shapes started hitting generic_matmul after the heuristic flip.

maya: KV cache hit rate also tanked at the same timestamp — from ~82% -> ~55% in the affected pool. That would increase small-batch churn too.

ryan: Batch metrics show avg batch size drop: `batch_size_avg: 6.4 -> 4.7` and small_batch_ratio `0.42 -> 0.68` around the same window. That aligns with fallback to slower kernel + smaller batches.

infra-bot: deploybot: rollout pulse-window-v2 to fleet ``canary->prod`` completed at 2149001050 (deploy id: dpl-2149).

diego: Any PRs touching TTL/prefetch or packing cost calc? Could be two changes colliding.

ashley: PR #3456 changed KV prefetch TTL from 30s -> 5s (intended to reduce stale entries). That landed earlier in the day. I have a quick staging revert where I only restored TTL and p99 returned to baseline.

maya: Right — lowering TTL explains the KV hit drop. Combined with pulse-window's new fallback thresholds it forces more cold batches.

ryan: Suggested mitigation: revert pulse-window threshold or disable fallback to generic kernel for shapes that should map to fast_attention. Example flags: `--pulse-window-threshold=0.6` or `--pulse-window-enable-fallback=false`. Also revert TTL to 30s.

ashley: I ran a quick local replay with the following commands to reproduce and gather traces:
```
# replay a 10s span around the incident
./replay_tool --trace-ids aa12,aa13,aa14 --dump-profile /tmp/pulse-debug.pb
# kernel debug logging
kubectl logs runtime-pod-3 -c runtime --since=5m | grep "kernel_selected" | tail -n 50
```
Attached sample trace ids: aa12, aa13, aa14.

diego: Thanks. If staging revert fixed it we should hotfix prod. @ryan can you prepare a quick rollback patch for TTL + pulse-window flag? Keep canary window short.

ryan: I'll prepare a hotfix to set `pulse_window_enabled=false` and reset `kv_prefetch_ttl=30` then roll to a small canary. ETA 12m.

ashley: After staging revert, metrics immediately improved (p99 back to baseline, throughput restored). I'll monitor once you roll.

infra-bot: deploybot: starting deploy dpl-hotfix-214900 to shard group A (canary) at 2149003200.

sre-ops: Creating incident INC-2149 and paging oncall. Noting customer impact for a small subset of requests.

diego: Good plan. After hotfix we should add a regression test that asserts kernel selection stability for common shapes when TTL changes. Also open a follow-up to reassess packing cost estimator — it's deciding fallback too aggressively.

ashley: Agreed. I'll open a ticket with collected traces and the staging revert results. For now, monitor dashboard and tag me if p99 goes above baseline.

ryan: Canary finished and looks good — pushing to prod.

infra-bot: deploybot: deploy dpl-hotfix-214900 completed at 2149004600.

ashley: Current metrics (2149004700): p99 back within +10ms of baseline, throughput recovered. Leaving this thread open until we have a postmortem and follow-up work.

sre-ops: Incident INC-2149 created and assigned to ashley/ryan/diego.

diego: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: schedule a kernel-routing review next week and add an automated unit test for TTL/kernel stability. :thumbsup:
